# Lua API

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_lua_doc.lua from the documented code, do not edit -->

What the app offers scripts, file by file. How scripts work: [lua_scripts.md](lua_scripts.md).

- C++: a comment tagged `\lua` documents the code below it.
  - `register_function("web.fetch", …)`: scripts call `workflow.web.fetch`, the parameters of the lambda are theirs. `std::optional` is a value or nil, `std::vector` a list, `std::map` a table.
  - `register_setting(*settings().name)`: scripts see the setting at `workflow.setting` followed by its path, the first argument of the `create_setting` of `name`, with the setting functions of `lua::state`.
  - A manifest struct with the `id` "scripture.read": a script offers the function "scripture.read", its input and output are tables of the keys of the `lua::field`s.
- Lua: a `---` comment documents the function below it. In `interface_util.lua`, `util.split` is `util.split` for scripts, in `usx.lua` `usx.parse` is `scripts.usx.parse`, in `init.lua` `interface.load` is `load`. Files named `system_*` are not seen by scripts.

## bibstd/lua/internal/init.lua

setmetatable of scripts. A finalizer fails: Lua runs it without hooks, the shutdown could not stop it.

- Returns `table`

```lua
function interface.setmetatable(table, metatable)
```

load of scripts. Text only, damaged bytecode crashes the app. By default the chunk gets globals of its own.

- Returns the loaded chunk, or nil and the error

```lua
function interface.load(chunk, name, _, environment)
```

## bibstd/lua/internal/interface_util.lua

`util.log_debug(...)`
`util.log_info(...)`
`util.log_warning(...)`
`util.log_error(...)`
Writes to the app log at that level. Scripts have no console and no print.

- `...`: the values, written like print writes them

```lua
for _, level in ipairs({ "debug", "info", "warning", "error" }) do
  local log = root.system["log_" .. level]
  util["log_" .. level] = function(...)
    log(text(...))
  end
end
```

- Returns the parts of `s` between the occurrences of the plain string `separator`, empty parts are kept

```lua
function util.split(s, separator)
```

- Returns `s` without the white space at its start and end

```lua
function util.trim(s)
```

- Returns true if `s` starts with `prefix`

```lua
function util.starts_with(s, prefix)
```

- Returns true if `s` ends with `suffix`

```lua
function util.ends_with(s, suffix)
```

- Returns the keys of `t` as list, in no particular order

```lua
function util.keys(t)
```

- Returns true if a value of `t` equals `value`

```lua
function util.contains(t, value)
```

- Returns the list of `f` applied to every element of the list `t`

```lua
function util.map(t, f)
```

- Returns the elements of the list `t` for which `predicate` is true, in their order

```lua
function util.filter(t, predicate)
```

- Returns a deep copy of `value`, tables referenced more than once stay shared in the copy and cycles are kept

```lua
function util.copy(value)
```

- Returns readable text of `value`, tables are expanded with sorted keys

```lua
function util.dump(value)
```

- Returns the value at `path` of sections separated by "." in what scripts see, nil if a section is missing

```lua
function util.at(path)
```

- Returns the element tree of the XML document `text`, or nil and the reason if it is not well-formed. An element
is a table { name, attributes, children }, its attributes by name, its children elements and texts in their order.
Comments, processing instructions and the document type are left out, CDATA sections are text.

```lua
function util.parse_xml(text)
```

- Returns the text of the element `element` of util.parse_xml and its descendants, with
`without_layout` the texts of white space only left out, which lay a document out

```lua
function util.xml_text(element, without_layout)
```

## bibstd/lua/internal/system_util.lua

Remove what is at `path` of sections separated by "." in what scripts see, e.g. a function taken back, and the
tables on its way it leaves empty.

```lua
function util.remove(path)
```

## bibstd/lua/state.hpp

- Returns the value of the setting

```cpp
  node.set_function(
    names::function_get,
    function_cast(
      [&setting]() -> erased_type { return framework::create_setting_value_converter<T, erased_type>()(setting.value()); },
      registered
    )
  );
```

Changes the setting, like the user does in the settings.

- `value`: the new value
- Returns false if the setting rejected `value` or limited it to its range

```cpp
  node.set_function(
    names::function_set,
    function_cast(
      [&setting](const erased_type& value) -> bool
      { return setting.value(framework::create_setting_value_converter<erased_type, T>()(value)); },
      registered
    )
  );
```

- Returns the text shown after the value, e.g. its unit, or an empty text

```cpp
  node.set_function(names::function_postfix, function_cast([&setting]() { return setting.postfix; }, registered));
  return registration{data_, p, std::move(registered)};
```

## bibstd/workflow/workflow_bible_ref_lookup.hpp

A script that offers this and `lookup.url` opens references in the browser. `Lookup > Scripts` chooses the
script by its name. Until the user chooses, the app uses the script with the most translations. Respect the terms
of use of the web pages a script reads.

- `language`: the language of the user, `english` or `german`
- Returns names the translations to choose from in `Lookup > Translations`, may be empty. The app shows them as
they are, so the bundled scripts offer full names, e.g. `Lutherbibel`, and map them to url abbreviations.

- Returns defaults the translations used until the user chooses some

```cpp
  struct translations_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"lookup.translations"};
    using input = lua::script_table<lua::field<"language", std::string>>;
    using output = lua::script_table<
      lua::field<"names", std::vector<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"defaults", std::optional<std::vector<std::string>>>>;
  };
```

For a reference over several chapters the app asks once per chapter and opens each url in its own tab.

- `translations`: the chosen translations, in the order chosen
- `book`: the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`
- `chapter`: the chapter
- `verse_begin`: the first verse
- `verse_end`: the last verse
- Returns url the web page that shows the verses, or none. The app opens only a valid `http` or `https` url, so
encode characters that are not ASCII.

```cpp
  struct url_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"lookup.url"};
    using input = lua::script_table<
      lua::field<"translations", std::vector<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"book", std::string>,
      lua::field<"chapter", std::int64_t>,
      lua::field<"verse_begin", std::int64_t>,
      lua::field<"verse_end", std::int64_t>>;
    using output = lua::script_table<lua::field<"url", std::optional<std::string>>>;
  };
```

## bibstd/workflow/workflow_cache.cpp

Reads a text value from a cache. A cache keeps its values after the app closes. Each cache is the SQLite file
`cache/<name>.sqlite` in the local data folder, and other programs may read and change it. A cache that fails is
logged and holds nothing.

- `name`: the cache, made of letters, digits, `_` and `-`. Each script uses its own cache.
- `key`: the key of the value
- Returns the value, or `nil` if there is none

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "cache.get", [this](const std::string& name, const std::string& key) { return get(util::identifier{name}, key); }
       )
```

Writes a text value to a cache, see `workflow.cache.get`.

- `name`: the cache
- `key`: the key of the value
- `value`: the value, `nil` removes the key

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "cache.set",
         [this](const std::string& name, const std::string& key, std::optional<std::string> value)
         { set(util::identifier{name}, key, std::move(value)); }
       );
```

## bibstd/workflow/workflow_scripture.cpp

The name of the default scripture, `Scripture > Default name`, `nil` for none. Functions called with `nil` as
scripture name use it, so without a default scripture they find no scripture.

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_setting(*settings().default_scripture_name)
```

The versification for scriptures that have none, including those of scripts,
`Scripture > Fallback versification`.

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_setting(*settings().fallback_versification)
```

- Returns the number of scriptures, including those of scripts

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function("scripture.scripture_count", [this]() { return scripture_count(); })
```

- Returns the identifiers of all books, e.g. `john`

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.book_identifiers",
         []() { return util::enum_names<bible::book_id>() | std::ranges::to<std::vector<std::string>>(); }
       )
```

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its name, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.name",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name)
         { return information({{scripture_name}}).transform([](const auto& info) { return info.name; }); }
       )
```

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its abbreviation, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.abbreviation",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name)
         { return information({{scripture_name}}).transform([](const auto& info) { return info.abbreviation; }); }
       )
```

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its language, or `nil` if there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.language",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name)
         { return information({{scripture_name}}).transform([](const auto& info) { return info.language; }); }
       )
```

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- Returns its copyright, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.copyright",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name)
         { return information({{scripture_name}}).and_then([](const auto& info) { return info.copyright; }); }
       )
```

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id`: the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the abbreviation of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.book_abbreviation",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name, const std::string& book_id)
         {
           return book_information({{scripture_name}}, book_id_of(book_id))
             .transform([](const auto& names) { return names.abbreviation; });
         }
       )
```

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id`: the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the short name of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.book_short_name",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name, const std::string& book_id)
         {
           return book_information({{scripture_name}}, book_id_of(book_id))
             .transform([](const auto& names) { return names.short_name; });
         }
       )
```

An unknown book raises an error.

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id`: the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- Returns the long name of the book, or `nil` if it has none or there is no such scripture

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.book_long_name",
         [this](const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name, const std::string& book_id)
         {
           return book_information({{scripture_name}}, book_id_of(book_id))
             .transform([](const auto& names) { return names.long_name; });
         }
       )
```

A script that asks for a passage of its own scripture calls itself.

- `scripture_name`: the scripture, `nil` for the default scripture
- `book_id`: the identifier of the book, e.g. `john`
- `chapter`: the chapter
- `verse`: the verse
- Returns the verse with the markup of the app, or `nil` and the reason, e.g. `scripture not found`

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function(
         "scripture.passage",
         [this](
           const std::optional<std::string>& scripture_name,
           const std::string& book_id,
           std::uint32_t chapter,
           std::uint32_t verse
         )
         {
           const auto reference = bible::reference::create_unguarded(book_id_of(book_id), chapter, verse);
           const auto params = passage_params_t{.reference = reference, .scripture_name = scripture_name};
           return passage(params).transform([](const auto& result) { return result.passage.content; });
```

## bibstd/workflow/workflow_scripture.hpp

A script that offers all four `scripture` manifests offers scriptures, and several scripts may do so.
The app lists them with its other scriptures, named after the script, e.g. `LUT (Bibleserver)`, and uses the
fallback versification for them. Respect the copyright of the translations.

- Returns names the scriptures the script offers, e.g. `{ "ABC" }`

```cpp
  struct names_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"scripture.names"};
    using input = lua::script_table<>;
    using output = lua::script_table<lua::field<"names", std::vector<std::string>>>;
  };
```

Information about a scripture.

- `name`: one of the names the script offers
- Returns abbreviation its abbreviation
- Returns language its language
- Returns copyright its copyright, shown below the verses

```cpp
  struct information_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"scripture.information"};
    using input = lua::script_table<lua::field<"name", std::string>>;
    using output = lua::script_table<
      lua::field<"abbreviation", std::optional<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"language", std::optional<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"copyright", std::optional<std::string>>>;
  };
```

The names of a book in a scripture.

- `name`: one of the names the script offers
- `book`: the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`
- Returns abbreviation its abbreviation
- Returns short_name its short name, shown in the app. Without one the app shows the identifier.
- Returns long_name its long name

```cpp
  struct book_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"scripture.book"};
    using input = lua::script_table<lua::field<"name", std::string>, lua::field<"book", std::string>>;
    using output = lua::script_table<
      lua::field<"abbreviation", std::optional<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"short_name", std::optional<std::string>>,
      lua::field<"long_name", std::optional<std::string>>>;
  };
```

A verse. The app asks for every verse it shows and keeps nothing,
so the script may ask `workflow.cache` first.

- `name`: one of the names the script offers
- `book`: the identifier of the app, e.g. `john`
- `chapter`: the chapter
- `verse`: the verse
- Returns text its plain text. The app shows markup of a web page as text.
- Returns error shown in place of a verse without `text.` Without one the app shows `verse not found`.

```cpp
  struct passage_manifest final
  {
    static inline const util::path id{"scripture.passage"};
    using input = lua::script_table<
      lua::field<"name", std::string>,
      lua::field<"book", std::string>,
      lua::field<"chapter", std::int64_t>,
      lua::field<"verse", std::int64_t>>;
    using output = lua::script_table<lua::field<"text", std::optional<std::string>>, lua::field<"error", std::optional<std::string>>>;
  };
  // clang-format on
```

## bibstd/workflow/workflow_web.cpp

How long a failed url is not requested again, `Web > Pause after a failure`. With 0 s a script may
request a failed url again right away.

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_setting(*settings().retry_pause)
```

Fetches a web page. The script waits for the page, and other scripts wait too. During
`Web > Pause after a failure` a failed url is not requested again, it returns the same failure.

- `url`: the address of the page, http or https
- Returns the content of the page, or `nil` and the reason: `invalid_url`, `not_found` (HTTP 404 or 410),
`timeout` (after 30 s), `init_failed` or `request_failed`

```cpp
    << workflow_script_->register_function("web.fetch", [this](const std::string& url) { return fetch(url); });
```
